themes_detail.label: Tree Die-Off Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints exploded to 9 this past week versus a 0.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1700% spike (z-score: 8.5)—signaling either a disease outbreak, pest infestation, or environmental stress affecting Upper West Side street canopy this week.
evidence: 9 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1700% increase, z-score: 8.5)
This represents the single largest statistical spike in the dataset by percentage
Suggests concentrated, acute environmental event rather than baseline maintenance issue
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about whether a specific pathogen, pest, or weather event is killing trees across the district
Canvass neighborhoods to document which streets are most affected and what residents are observing

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks spiked to 12 complaints last week compared to 1.1 weekly average—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.98)—suggesting new overcrowding, amplified events, or unmanaged activity at UWS parks this week.
evidence: 12 park noise complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% increase, z-score: 7.98)
Second-highest spike by z-score in this week's data
Concentrated timing suggests discrete event or condition rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Identify which specific parks are generating complaints (Riverside, Central Park edges, etc.) and what activities are causing noise
Interview Parks Enforcement officers about whether they are adequately staffed to manage current park usage

themes_detail.label: Curb and Asphalt Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 16 last week from a 3.0-complaint weekly baseline—a 433% spike (z-score: 10.61)—indicating rapid street infrastructure failure across the Upper West Side this week, potentially linked to winter weather or deferred maintenance.
evidence: 16 curb condition complaints last week vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% increase, z-score: 10.61)
Highest z-score spike in the dataset, indicating most statistically anomalous event
Street Condition complaints also chronically high (1009 over 90 days), suggesting broader infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: File FOIL request to DOT for emergency repair data and budget allocation to CD107 to assess whether this is reactive or part of a planned infrastructure program
Document specific street blocks with worst curb damage and interview residents about pedestrian safety hazards

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Spike
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints spiked to 8 last week versus a 1.0-complaint weekly average—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.72)—raising urgent questions about whether renovation/demolition activity (1,173 DOB permits filed this quarter, including 7 demolitions) is releasing hazardous materials into residential buildings this week.
evidence: 8 asbestos complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score: 5.72)
1,173 active DOB permits in the district (last 90 days), including 7 full demolitions and 1,083 alterations—highest permitting activity on record
Temporal correlation: heavy construction + asbestos spike suggests inadequate remediation compliance during renovations
reporting_angles: Investigate whether DOB is adequately inspecting asbestos abatement during the current construction surge; request inspection violation data
Interview affected residents about which buildings triggered asbestos complaints and whether they were notified of hazards

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Outages
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints jumped to 26 two weeks ago from a 10.9-complaint weekly average—a 139% increase (z-score: 4.49)—pointing to a localized power or maintenance issue affecting neighborhood safety and pedestrian visibility over the past 2 weeks.
evidence: 26 street light complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 10.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (139% increase, z-score: 4.49)
Timing suggests either weather event, utility infrastructure failure, or maintenance backlog
This signal is declining (was 2 weeks ago, not this week), suggesting either resolution or normalization
reporting_angles: Contact Con Edison to determine if there was a transformer or service outage 2 weeks ago and estimated restoration timeline
Query DOT on street light maintenance schedules and whether the spike has resolved or represents ongoing darkness
